title: Progressive geo-aware version pinning with hedged fallback and A/B decay rules
creator: Priya Sethi
description:
Problem: We need a predictable and low-risk approach for progressive model version rollouts that respects customer region (geo) preferences, capacity tiers, and provides a deterministic hedging strategy when preferred variants are unavailable. Current route resolution is per-request and does not encode a decaying A/B split or hedged fallback that balances user affinity, regional capacity constraints, and variant quality regressions.

Goal: Define product-level policy primitives and surface them in the Console so teams can: 1) pin sessions/users to a model version with TTL and decay; 2) run canary or A/B rollouts that are geo-aware (region, region tier) and respect capacity tiers; 3) define explicit hedges to fallback variants (e.g., quantized, smaller, or older checkpoint) with clear cost/latency tradeoffs; 4) produce deterministic logs and metrics for rollback decisioning.

This ticket captures the PM proposal, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, telemetry requirements, and the dependencies we need from engineering and design to implement the feature end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: Console exposes a "progressive pinning" toggle when creating a rollout: options include TTL-based session pin (seconds), decay window (hours), and deterministic entropy seed to ensure reproducible A/B allocation.

Routing decision follows: 1) pinned variant if TTL active; 2) deterministic cohort A/B assignment if in active rollout; 3) region-tier-aware preferred route if capacity available; 4) hedged fallback variant if preferred variant unavailable or latency SLO breached.
Teams can configure an ordered list of fallback variants and a fallback budget (max additional latency or cost multiplier) per rollout.
Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-variant latency P50/P95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, and session-affinity churn rate broken down by region and tier.

A single canonical log line emitted per request with fields: request_id, resolved_variant, reason_code (PIN/AB/REGION/FALLBACK), route_priority, and shard_hint. (Instrumentation contract agreed with ENG).
Support for an opt-in 'shadowing window' where the new variant receives a copy of traffic for offline evaluation before being used as primary for any cohort.
Integration tests demonstrating deterministic A/B split reproducibility across edge failures and restarts.
Rollout can be aborted and traffic can be reverted to previous variant instantly via Console with telemetry preserved for the last 24 hours.
decision_notes: We selected a hybrid pin-and-decay model: pins are strong but time-bounded, cohort assignment uses a deterministic hash of (session_id or user_id + rollout_id + salt) so that rebalancing only occurs when TTLs expire or rollout config changes. Hedged fallback will be ordered and bounded by a fallback budget. For region preferences, we treat 'preferred region' as a soft constraint with higher priority than variant selection but lower than pin TTL. This ordering preserves UX for pinned sessions while enabling graceful degradation under regional capacity pressure.

acceptance_tests: Create a rollout in Console with progressive pinning enabled; issue requests from multiple simulated regions and verify pinned sessions remain on target variant until TTL expiry.
Trigger capacity saturation in a region and validate that hedged fallback is used and logged with correct reason_code and fallback variant id.
Run the same session through a restart of the router (simulate process restart) and confirm cohort assignment is deterministic and unchanged for unexpired TTLs.
Verify shadowing window traffic is delivered to the new variant but not counted as primary; offline comparison metrics are populated.
Abort rollout mid-way and confirm Console flips traffic back immediately while retaining historical metrics for 24 hours.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): 0%->5% shadowing for 72 hours in us-west1, gather latencies and correctness; Phase 2 (canary): 1% A/B in us-west1 and europe-west with progressive pin TTL=24h and decay=48h; Phase 3 (scale): expand to additional regions and release to 50% cohort if no regressions. If any P95 latency regression >20% or error rate increases by >0.5% for 1 hour, auto-abort to previous variant.
fallback_policy_spec: A rollout config contains 'fallbacks' ordered array: [variantA-quant, variantA-small, variantA-prev]. Each fallback has metadata: max_cost_multiplier (string), max_added_latency_ms (string). Route resolver will attempt the next fallback if backend returns CAPACITY_EXCEEDED or observed latency > max_added_latency_ms. A separate 'hedge' flag controls whether fallback is used only for read traffic or both read/write.
open_questions: Should pins be user-level or session-level by default? (Design prefers session-level with opt-in user-level).
How do we surface multi-variant hedging cost estimates in Console without leaking internal cost models?
Do we expose an API to mutate the deterministic salt for cohort hashing? Changing salt causes cohort drift — how should that be gated?
What is the exact retention period for canonical routing logs exposed to customers vs. internal SRE?
